content: 1. The therapeutic effects of penicillins may be reduced when used concurrently with tetracyclines. This interaction occurs due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, particularly with drugs like sarecycline and piperacillin. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. 2. Tetracyclines can interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Close monitoring is advised to detect any decrease in the therapeutic effects of penicillins when co-administered with tetracyclines. 3. Polysaccharide iron can reduce the absorption and effectiveness of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 4. Products containing multivalent cations, such as calcium, magnesium, or iron, may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, leading to reduced efficacy. It is advised to separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 5. Sarecycline can increase the levels or effects of drugs like pomalidomide, posaconazole, pravastatin, prednisone, quinidine, quinine, ranolazine, rifampin, rifaximin, riociguat, risperidone, ritonavir, saxagliptin, silodosin, simvastatin, sirolimus, sitagliptin, tacrolimus, temsirolimus, teniposide, tenofovir (AF and DF), testosterone, tolvaptan, topotecan, trabectedin, velpatasvir, vemurafenib, venetoclax, verapamil, vinblastine, vincristine, vincristine liposomal, and voxilaprevir. This occurs via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are required to manage potential toxicities, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. 6. Sodium acid phosphate, sodium bicarbonate, sodium citrate/citric acid, sodium phosphate rectal, and magnesium-containing products can decrease the absorption and effectiveness of sarecycline by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 7. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate can reduce sarecycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. It is advised to avoid or use alternative drugs. Tetracyclines should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents to prevent chelation with magnesium. 8. Sarecycline increases the effects of rocuronium and succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism, which may lead to respiratory depression. Alternative drugs should be considered, and close monitoring is essential. 9. Oral retinoids, when used with tetracyclines, may increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri or intracranial hypertension. This combination should be avoided, and patients should be closely monitored for symptoms. 10. Zinc can decrease the absorption and effectiveness of sarecycline by binding to it in the GI tract. It is recommended to separate the administration of oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts by at least 2 hours. 11. Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported with nearly all antibacterial agents, including tetracyclines. The severity can range from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. If CDAD is suspected or confirmed, ongoing antibacterial therapy not directed against C. difficile should be discontinued, and appropriate treatment measures should be initiated. 12. Central nervous system side effects, such as light-headedness, dizziness, or vertigo, have been reported with tetracycline use. Patients experiencing these symptoms should be cautioned about engaging in activities requiring alertness, such as driving.
